evals.prompt: List the five severity levels the AWS Config cost optimization skill uses for its findings, in order from most to least urgent. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Lists CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO in that order.
assertions: The five severity levels are given in order from most to least urgent (CRITICAL first, INFO last)

evals.prompt: For an AWS Config resource type that changes many times per day, which recording mode is usually cheaper - continuous or daily - and why? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Explains that daily recording is usually cheaper for high-churn resources because it bills at most one configuration item per resource per day, whereas continuous recording bills every change, so continuous can cost more overall despite its lower per-CI price.
assertions: The response identifies daily recording as usually cheaper for a high-churn resource
The response explains that continuous recording bills every change while daily bills at most one configuration item per resource per day
The response notes that daily's higher per-CI price is outweighed by the once-per-day cap for high-churn resources

evals.prompt: My AWS Config setup has two conformance packs - a NIST 800-53 pack and a PCI DSS pack - that share about 40% of their rules. Separate auditors consume the NIST compliance report and the PCI compliance report independently. To cut Config evaluation costs, should I merge them into one combined conformance pack? Explain the tradeoff. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Advises NOT merging the packs when both frameworks must be attested independently. Explains that AWS Config tracks compliance per pack and the shared rules deliberately map to different framework controls, so merging destroys the separate per-framework compliance reporting the auditors rely on. Treats the overlapping-rule evaluation cost as a small, deliberate cost of dual attestation (an INFO observation), and recommends verifying the compliance consumer before any consolidation.
assertions: The response advises against merging the two packs into one (does not recommend consolidation as the fix)
The response explains that compliance is tracked per pack and separate per-framework attestation/reporting would be lost by merging
The response characterizes the overlapping-rule evaluation cost as small relative to the lost per-framework reporting, or frames the overlap as acceptable/INFO rather than waste

evals.prompt: In AWS Config I have a standalone acm-certificate-expiration-check rule with a 14-day threshold, and my conformance pack also includes acm-certificate-expiration-check but with a 90-day threshold. Is the standalone rule just a duplicate I should delete to save on evaluations? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the standalone rule is NOT a pure duplicate because its 14-day threshold differs from the pack's 90-day threshold - it enforces a stricter, different requirement. Recommends flagging the threshold conflict for the customer to reconcile rather than deleting the standalone rule outright, and only removing a standalone rule when its source identifier AND parameters match the pack's and it serves no distinct purpose.
assertions: The response states the standalone rule is not simply a duplicate because its threshold differs from the pack's
The response recommends reconciling or reviewing the threshold conflict rather than deleting the standalone rule outright
The response ties the duplicate determination to matching parameters/thresholds, not just the rule name or source identifier

evals.prompt: For an AWS Config cost optimization review of account 123456789012, state the report artifact filename you would generate (use today's date in YYYY-MM-DD form). Do not run the review.
evals.expected_output: Proposes an artifact name of the form config-cost-optimization-123456789012-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md.

assertions.text: The response proposes an artifact filename of the form config-cost-optimization-<account-id>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md

evals.prompt: Help me tune the parameter group on my Amazon RDS PostgreSQL instance to improve query performance.
evals.expected_output: The AWS Config cost optimization skill should not activate - this is an RDS performance tuning request unrelated to AWS Config cost.
assertions: The response addresses RDS parameter group / performance tuning and does not steer the user into an AWS Config cost optimization review
